title: Curriculum (Prospective Students) - NUS Computing
description: # Bachelor of Computing (Honours) in Computer Science. The Bachelor of Computing (Honours) in Computer Science or BComp (CS) programme aims to nurture students for a rewarding computing career in various industry sectors. * Strong knowledge of computer science foundations and fundamentals, including (a) familiarity with common computer science themes and principles, (b) high-level understanding of systems as a whole, (c) understanding of the theoretical underpinnings of computer science and their influences in practice. The Bachelor of Computing (Computer Science) programme, BComp(CS), requires at least 160 units. Note that least 80% of the unit requirements in a Bachelor programme’s major (i.e. Programme Requirements) must be at level 1000 to 4000. * Complete at least 12 units at level-4000 or above * Complete at least 6 units and at most 12 units of Industry Experience courses * Students with GPA of 4.00 or higher may opt to replace the Industry Experience courses with the programme’s dissertation course (i.e. CP4101).

title: Computer Science - NUS Computing
description: # Bachelor of Computing in Computer Science (with Honours\*). These are just a few of the opportunities you’ll have as a Computer Science student at NUS. As part of your education, you will build and develop applications, while learning the theoretical foundations of Computer Science that make it all possible. The end goal of our Computer Science programme is to prepare candidates for a rewarding career as computing professionals. Our project-based approach means that you will build a portfolio that you can showcase to employers to demonstrate your achievements as a software developer and engineer. A career in Computer Science gives you the opportunity to build the future. Our Computer Science programme offers a wide spectrum of electives across many sub-areas to give students the flexibility to build up expertise for different job domains:. Learn how to build efficient distributed systems that are able to handle large amounts of real-time data for data mining and machine learning.

title: Modules I took at NUS: School of Computing | by Royce Ho | Medium
description: # Modules I took at NUS: School of Computing | by Royce Ho | Medium. # Modules I took at NUS: School of Computing. ## Year 1–3. This is a quick recap of the modules I took at NUS for my major, Computer Science, from 2019–2021, and my experience may differ from many others. Majority of modules taken in year 1 and 2 and similar for most students, and in year 3 and 4 we are quite free to choose from the various focus areas offered. > Part 1: What is NUS Computer Science really about? 3.   Year 2, Sem 1: CS2103T, CS2100, CS2105, CS2101. It was a very tough module for the majority, and not taught in the best way. Math and stats mods were offered by the Faculty of Science (now renamed as College of Humanities and Sciences) and it felt that close to no effort was put into these modules by the teaching team.

title: A brief guide for potential NUS Computer Science undergraduates
description: Specific references in this article about NUS and the computing faculty may be outdated - please contact me if there’s information that should be updated. As there has been growing interest in CS undergraduate courses over the past few years, I would like to share my experience as a CS major at National University of Singapore, and also shed light on the common misconceptions that people may have. This essay will also be focussed on National University of Singapore’s curriculum and programmes, because I’m most familiar with it. Prior to this, I graduated from Ngee Ann Polytechnic with a Diploma in Network Systems & Security. A quick search on Wikipedia on a network protocol algorithm, Djikstra’s Shortest Path, inundated me with so much math that it quickly made me realize that a CS education will provide the foundational theoretical knowledge to understand these algorithms. CS is the science of computational processes, like how Physics is the science of nature.
